clue.text: Material collected by the old man, socialist geared up

indicators.note: the fabric word is gathered up inside the word for father, held between its letters

parts.note: the old man is a familiar term for father, PA
rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
red is the usual crossword label for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A family scene: dad gathers up some cloth while a left-wing activist gets ready for action.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone geared up is equipped and ready, the same state as being made ready in advance.

clue.text: Express discontent about timber used for furniture

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning
pine is a softwood commonly made into furniture

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about the wood chosen for their furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface ties 'about' to the complaint; in fact it is the short Latin-style word for concerning, set at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is an old-fashioned verb meaning to fret or complain, a synonym for voicing discontent.

clue.text: Orient or East maybe?

definitions.meaning: to orient is to aim or direct something, as you do when you aim a camera
east is one of the compass directions, an example signalled by maybe

explanation.surface: A question of geography: is the Orient simply another name for the East?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orient' and 'East' look like the same place, but the first is a verb meaning to aim and the second an example of a compass bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiming something is a verb sense; a compass bearing such as East is a noun sense of the same word.

clue.text: Quiet about men losing head or feeling bitter?

indicators.note: the word for quiet goes around the shortened men, holding it inside

parts.note: restful means calm and quiet

indicators.note: the word men drops its first letter

explanation.surface: A question of whether quiet surrounding a group of men leaves them aggrieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a container signal here, and 'losing head' acts on the word men itself, not on any synonym for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A resentful person nurses a grievance, so the adjective describes a state of bitterness.

clue.text: Girls less mad, having changed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Some young women have calmed down and are less angry than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having changed' rearranges the letters of LESS MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an archaic or literary word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Chatter with teacher before start of tutorial

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

indicators.note: only the opening letter of tutorial is used

explanation.surface: Idle talk with the tutor just as a tutorial begins.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for talking at length; 'before' simply sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit is to talk on and on, a synonym for idle prattle.

clue.text: One getting up only a bit of the staircase

definitions.meaning: a person who gets out of bed, early or late

definitions.text: only a bit of the staircase
definitions.meaning: the vertical board between two treads of a stair

explanation.surface: Someone climbing just part of the stairs on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: An early bird is an example of someone who leaves bed; the upright panel of each step carries the same name.

clue.text: Deceive head, showing outspoken nature

parts.note: to bluff is to deceive by pretence
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names like Sheerness

explanation.surface: Fooling the boss reveals a person's frank character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a geographical headland, NESS, not a person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluffness is blunt, frank directness of manner, a synonym for being outspoken.

clue.text: Mingle in area around end of lane

indicators.note: the word for area surrounds the final letter of lane

parts.note: a tract is a stretch or area of land

indicators.note: only the last letter of lane is used

explanation.surface: People mix in a neighbourhood near the bottom of a lane.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to act on one another socially, a synonym for mixing with people.

clue.text: Plunder Mars

definitions.meaning: noun: goods taken by force, loot

explanation.surface: Looting on the red planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' looks like the planet but is the verb to mar.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is a synonym for the noun; damaging or ruining is the verb sense.

clue.text: Insect, very large, left for doctor to get hold of

indicators.note: the doctor abbreviation grips the other letters between its two

parts.note: MO is the abbreviation for medical officer
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
quit means left or departed

explanation.surface: A huge bug that walked off, leaving a physician to catch it.
explanation.definitionFit: The biting gnat that spreads malaria is a familiar example of a flying insect.

clue.text: Illustration of batting position

parts.note: in cricket a batsman at the crease is in
a stance is a way of standing, a posture

explanation.surface: A picture of where a cricketer stands to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is said to be 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example that illustrates a point, a synonym for illustration.

clue.text: Improve group of students taking Religious Education

parts.note: RE is the school subject abbreviation
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A class gets better by studying Religious Education.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to make better by correcting faults, a synonym for improve.

clue.text: Magazine has a few words on severe punishment

parts.note: Life was a famous American picture magazine
a sentence is a short string of words

explanation.surface: A magazine runs a short piece about harsh penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprisonment for the rest of one's days is the harshest jail term in many countries.

clue.text: Put off rising — importance said to be to plan for attack

parts.note: a lie-in is staying in bed late, delaying getting up

indicators.note: the word for importance is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: weight means importance or significance

explanation.surface: Staying in bed is supposedly so important it counts as a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide and wait in ambush is an idiom for preparing a surprise attack.

clue.text: Unpleasant quality of inn's seats wobbling about

indicators.note: unsteady seats suggest letters shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub's rickety chairs are a disagreeable feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbling about' rearranges the letters of INN'S SEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastiness is the abstract noun for being unpleasant or spiteful.

clue.text: Revenge of agent, gentleman turning up to get gangster?

parts.note: rep is short for representative, a sales agent

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so back to front

parts.note: sir is the title for a gentleman or knight
Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A salesman and a toff appear in search of revenge on a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses SIR to RIS in this down clue; the gangster is Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is a retaliatory act, a synonym for revenge.

clue.text: Tree experts?

parts.note: the tree is a family tree, so these experts trace ancestry rather than study woods

explanation.surface: Specialists in trees, such as botanists or arborists.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is not a plant but a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Researchers who trace family lineages build family trees, hence the jokey label.

clue.text: Fellow with limb stuck in jacket?

indicators.note: the limb goes inside the word for fellow

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a fellow
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A man has got his arm caught in his jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a jacket as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket is one example of an item of clothing.

clue.text: Cowboy to travel, carrying gold with companion

indicators.note: the word for travel holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to go is to travel
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A cowboy rides off with treasure and a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is a British honour, Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a South American cowboy of the pampas.

clue.text: British farm just one part of the business

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm

explanation.surface: A British farm is only one arm of a larger company.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a local office or division of a company, one part of it.

clue.text: Difficult to hide ring in secret store

indicators.note: the word for difficult conceals the ring letter within it

parts.note: hard means difficult
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: It is hard to conceal a ring in a stash.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a hidden stock of money or valuables, a synonym for a secret cache.

clue.text: Deceitful person going wrong way, boss in terminal situation

indicators.note: the word for a deceiver is read backwards

parts.note: a liar is a deceitful person
the head is the boss

explanation.surface: A dishonest man goes astray while his boss is in a fatal plight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal situation' sounds like a dying condition but means the end of a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A railhead is the point where a railway line ends, a terminus.

clue.text: Colouring agent used in kitchen, naturally

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the words kitchen and naturally

explanation.surface: A food colouring used in the kitchen, of natural origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish plant dye used on hair and skin.

clue.text: A daughter in flight for an adventure

indicators.note: the letters go within the word for flight

parts.note: escape means flight, fleeing

explanation.surface: A girl takes a plane journey looking for excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or reckless exploit, a synonym for an adventure.

clue.text: Girl is English, superior, and pleasant

parts.note: U means upper-class, socially superior, in British usage
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A description of an English woman who is refined and agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a British convention from the 1950s 'U and non-U' debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a female first name, an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Details I missed, looking back — will get criticised

indicators.note: the remaining letters are read from right to left
the I is left out of the word details

explanation.surface: Someone who overlooked particulars will be blamed when reviewing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' drops I from DETAILS to leave DETALS; 'looking back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be slated is British informal for being harshly criticised.

clue.text: One with a will to help others succeed?

definitions.text: One with a will to help others succeed?

parts.words: One with a will to help others succeed?
parts.note: a will here is a legal document, and to succeed is to inherit, so this person leaves property to heirs

explanation.surface: A determined helper keen on others' success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' is the legal document and 'succeed' means to inherit, not to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: The maker of a legal will lets heirs inherit, which is succession.
